parts.title: Spin a Hanging Magnet. Why Does It Stop the SAME Way? (Part 1) | Compass
parts.description:
Basil hangs his bar magnet on a string and spins it, again and again. Does it stop a different way every time, or the same way every time? Lock in your answer from last time, be the hanging magnet, test it in three places, spot Basil's mistake on the bench, and fly up to see the whole Earth. Part 1 of Primary 3 Science, Properties of Magnets: the compass.

In this part:
• Spin a hanging magnet: where does it stop? (last episode's dare)
• Be the hanging magnet: something you cannot see turns you back
• Look closer: the field, the classroom, a basin of water: the same line every time
• HOLD ON! On the bench, is it free?
• Look closer: how does the magnet know? The whole Earth
• Spot the hidden swallow!

Key words: freely suspended, North-South direction, Earth behaves like a magnet.
Watch Part 2: how a compass works, and what happens when a magnet comes close. Last episode: why a ring magnet floats in mid-air.

TheOneApp, Explained: Singapore primary science, made fun. Play along with Pip, Basil and Momo: show fingers to lock in, keep score on your hand, beat the Buddies!

Why does a hanging magnet always stop the same way? P3 Science, Chapter 6, Properties of Magnets (pp. 110 to 112): a freely suspended magnet comes to rest in the North-South direction; Earth behaves like a magnet with its own North and South poles, and it interacts with a freely suspended magnet; a compass can help us to find the direction, because when the needle inside the compass stops moving, it always points in the North-South direction of the Earth. The third episode of the Magnets theme. Also fits US NGSS 3-PS2-3 (Grade 3).
Safety and care: Keep magnets and phones away from compasses: they can turn the needle the wrong way. Bring a magnet close slowly, and never press it onto a compass. Never put a magnet in your mouth, and keep magnets away from little brothers and sisters. Go hiking with an adult. We look at swallows and sea turtles, and we do not touch them.
Try it at home: With an adult, tie a thread round the middle of a bar magnet and hang it from a wooden stick, away from anything made of steel. Spin it gently a few times. Which way does it stop? Check with a compass (or a compass app on a phone held well away from the magnet), and find which wall of your room faces North.
Hikers on Pulau Ubin and at MacRitchie Reservoir use a compass on the trails, and every ship in the Singapore Strait carries one, even at night.
Grade 3 pupils in the US learn it the same way (NGSS 3-PS2-3): magnets act on each other without touching, and a compass needle is a magnet that the Earth turns.

parts.title: Bring a Magnet Near a Compass. What Does the Needle DO? (Part 2) | Compass
parts.description:
A bar magnet comes close to a compass. Does nothing happen, does the needle turn, or does it spin forever? Lock in your answer, be the compass needle, learn how to use a compass at Pulau Ubin, spot the mistake in Momo's compass checklist, and find out if a compass works at night. Part 2 of Primary 3 Science, Properties of Magnets: the compass.

In this part:
• A magnet near a compass: what happens?
• Be the compass needle: pushed away, then pulled in
• Look closer: turn the compass, not the needle
• Showdown: Momo's compass checklist
• Look closer: a ship at night, a hiker in the fog
• A chant to remember it all
• Spot the hidden sea turtle!

Key words: needle, compass, tell the direction.
Watch Part 1 first! Next episode: can you turn an iron nail into a magnet?
